chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ismāʿīl ibn Mihrān, who said:

When Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام departed from al-Madīnah to Baghdād on the first of his two departures, I said to him at the time of his departure, “May I be your ransom, I fear for you on this journey, so to whom will the authority belong after you?” He turned his face toward me smiling and said, “The occultation is not where you supposed, in this year.”

Then when he was taken out a second time to al-Muʿtaṣim, I went to him and said to him, “May I be your ransom, you are departing, so to whom will this authority belong after you?” Then he wept until his beard became soaked. Then he turned to me and said, “At this time it is feared for me; the authority after me belongs to my son ʿAlī.”

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, the Imam being addressed in the narration
key_terms.ابْنِي عَلِيٍّ: my son ʿAlī, identified as the Imam after him
key_terms.الْأَمْرُ: the authority or command, referring here to the Imamate
key_terms.الْغَيْبَةُ: the occultation or absence from public access
key_terms.الْمُعْتَصِمِ: al-Muʿtaṣim, the Abbasid caliph to whom he was taken

ai.seo_question: How did Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام indicate that the Imamate after him would belong to his son ʿAlī عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith records a designation of the Imam after Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام during the circumstances of his summons to Baghdād. It distinguishes between the first departure, in which the feared event had not yet come, and the second, in which he explicitly states that the authority after him belongs to his son ʿAlī عليه السلام. The narration is significant in discussions of Imamate, succession, and the historical life of the Imams عليهم السلام.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin Mihran who said,

‘When Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> went out from Al-Medina to Baghdad during the first time from his<sup>asws</sup> two such exits, I said to him<sup>asws</sup> during his<sup>asws</sup> exiting, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! I fear upon you during this direction, so to whom would be the command (Imamate) after you<sup>asws</sup>?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> turned his<sup>asws</sup> face towards me smiling and said: ‘The Occultation isn’t to be during this year, where your thoughts are’.

So when they went out with him<sup>asws</sup> for the second time to Al-Mu’tasim (the Caliph), I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! You<sup>asws</sup> are going out, so to whom would this command (Imamate) be from after you<sup>asws</sup>?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> wept until his<sup>asws</sup> beard was soaked. Then he<sup>asws</sup> turned towards me and he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is what you had feared upon me<sup>asws</sup>. The command (Imamate) from after me<sup>asws</sup> is to my<sup>asws</sup> son<sup>asws</sup> Ali<sup>asws</sup>’ (10<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>).
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father that ’Isma‘il ibn Mihran who has said the following.

“When abu Ja‘far (a.s.) left Madina for Baghdad the first time of his two journeys on his leaving I said to him, “May Allah take my souls in service for your cause, I am afraid about you in this condition. To who, after you, will belong the task (Leadership with Divine Authority)?” He turned to me laughing and said, “The disappearance, as have thought, will not take place this year.

When he was about to be taken to al-Mu‘tasam (179/795 —became caliph 218/833 — 227/841), for the second time I went to him and said, “May Allah take my souls in service for your cause. You are leaving. To who, after you, will go this task Leadership with Divine Authority)?” He wept until his beard become soaked. He then turned to me and said, “This time you should be afraid about my life. The task (Leadership with Divine Authority) after me will go to my son Ali (a.s.).”
